findings.title: Map POI markers are raw OS color emoji (breaks the parchment/nautical art style)
findings.what: Every charted point-of-interest on the fullscreen Battle Map and the minimap is a full-color OS emoji glyph drawn with ctx.fillText: skull 💀 (forts), beer mug 🍺 (taverns), anchor ⚓ (shipwrecks), volcano 🌌/mountain ⛰️ (peaks), money bag 💰 (gold hoarder), moai 🗿 (standing stones), candle 🕯️ (mysterious stranger), crossed hammer ⚒️, crystal ball 🔮, hole 🕳️ (caves), tower 🗼. Glossy 3D Apple-style emoji clash hard with the flat dark-navy/gold parchment map and render completely differently (or as tofu boxes) across Windows/Linux/Android, so the map's look is non-deterministic and reads as a placeholder rather than stylized-AAA. SoT uses a cohesive set of engraved single-tone nautical icons.
findings.where: test-results/audit-noon2/map.png — icons on every island: Castaway Reach (skull+mug+anchor), Old Maw Caldera (volcano+moneybag+hammer), Skull Cove (crossed swords/hammer+moneybag), Smuggler's Rest (candle+moai+moneybag); also duplicated in the right-panel minimap.
findings.root_cause_guess: src/client/core/Game.ts:9607-9638 (renderBattleMap) draws POI markers as literal emoji string constants via ctx.fillText ('🌌', '⚓', '🗿', '💀', '🍺', '💰', '⚒️', '🔮', '🕯️', '🕳️', '🗼') with a generic 'serif' font.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the emoji with custom canvas-drawn vector glyphs (or a preloaded 1-bit icon sprite atlas) in the map's gold/bone palette (#f4e8c6 / #c9a84c) with a dark outline, so icons are monochrome, on-style, and identical on every platform. Keep the type→icon mapping but route it through a drawPoiIcon(ctx,type,x,y) helper instead of fillText(emoji).

findings.title: Fullscreen Battle Map: storm-timer chip overlaps the 'BATTLE MAP' title and duplicates the storm subtitle
findings.what: On the fullscreen map the canvas-drawn storm chip 'NEXT 1:36' (gold Georgia text in a dark box) is rendered in the exact top-left corner where the HTML #map-title 'BATTLE MAP' sits, so the two strings collide and overprint into an unreadable smear. Worse, that same storm countdown is ALSO shown correctly as the #map-subtitle 'NEXT STORM SHIFT IN 95S' in the top-right — so the colliding chip is fully redundant. The chip is correct for the minimap (its own top-left corner is empty) but should not be drawn under the fullscreen title.
findings.where: test-results/audit-noon2/map.png — top-left header: gold 'NEXT 1:36' bleeding through the white 'BATTLE MAP' title box; redundant 'NEXT STORM SHIFT IN 95S' sits top-right.
findings.root_cause_guess: renderBattleMap draws the storm chip unconditionally at canvas (8,8) — src/client/core/Game.ts:9580-9586 — for both minimap and fullscreen. In fullscreen the HTML overlay #map-title is positioned at top:18px/left:22px (index.html:1149-1156) over the same corner, and #map-subtitle already prints the storm timer. The code even has a comment (index.html:1122) acknowledging the (8,8) chip fights the corner.
findings.suggested_fix: Suppress the canvas storm chip when fullscreen (the HTML subtitle already covers it): guard the fillRect/fillText at 9580-9586 with `if (!fullscreen)`. Alternatively move the fullscreen chip below the title band (e.g. y offset ~48px) or center the #map-title.

findings.title: Ship flags and pennants are flat single-plane quads (stiff cardboard cloth)
findings.what: Every jolly-roger flag and masthead pennant is a single un-subdivided PlaneGeometry, so it reads as a flat rigid cardboard cutout with hard straight edges instead of billowing cloth. Only a whole-plane Y/Z rotation is animated (no per-segment ripple), which is especially obvious on the sloop's green pennant (a flat plus-sign shape) and the skull banner. SoT flags are segmented cloth with a visible traveling wave and a rippled trailing edge.
findings.where: test-results/audit-noon2/ship-3-sloop-deck.png (masthead: flat green pennant + flat green skull flag), test-results/audit-noon3/ship-1-brigantine-ext.png (red masthead flag), ship-2-galleon-ext.png.
findings.root_cause_guess: src/client/rendering/ShipRenderer.ts:2126-2127 (pennant = new THREE.PlaneGeometry(1.15 - m*0.12, 0.26)) and :2700 (flagGeo = new THREE.PlaneGeometry(0.85, 0.52)); animation at :3164-3167 only sets rotation.y/z on the whole mesh.
findings.suggested_fix: Subdivide the flag/pennant plane along its length (e.g. PlaneGeometry(w,h, 8..12, 1)) and drive a small sine traveling-wave in a vertex shader (or per-frame vertex update) anchored at the mast edge, amplitude scaled by wind.strength + ship speed, so the trailing edge ripples. Cheap and dramatically lifts the silhouette.

findings.title: Deep underwater renders as a near-black empty void (no god rays / seabed / particulate)
findings.what: Diving to depth collapses the whole frame to near-black with only a faint teal horizon line — there is no volumetric murk gradient, no god rays, no drifting particulate, and no visible seabed, so 'deep underwater' looks like a broken/empty render rather than the moody blue-green depths SoT shows. The deep fog target color is almost pure black (rgb 3,31,53) and the exponential density (0.018) fogs everything past ~80m to that color while lights/exposure are also driven down.
findings.where: test-results/audit-noon2/underwater-deep.png (entire frame black except a thin teal band). Shallow shot test-results/audit-noon2/underwater-shore.png also reads half above-water because the underwater blend only fully engages past ~1.45m depth.
findings.root_cause_guess: src/client/rendering/Renderer.ts:202 fogUnderwaterDeepColor = 0x031f35 (very dark navy) blended in at :473-474, plus waterFog density lerp to 0.018 at :476 and exposure/light dimming at :489-497; nothing adds god-ray/particulate/seabed detail underwater.
findings.suggested_fix: Lift fogUnderwaterDeepColor toward a murky teal (e.g. ~0x0a3a4a) and cap deep fog density lower (~0.010-0.012) so silhouettes survive; add a cheap underwater layer — a few animated god-ray planes or a scrolling caustic/particulate sprite field — and ensure the seabed mesh stays lit enough to read at depth. Keep it dark and moody but non-empty.

findings.title: Crew / player character reads as an untextured placeholder mannequin at the deck camera
findings.what: At the close third-person deck camera the pirate is a flat single-color coat with no texture/normal detail, a completely faceless skin-tone sphere for a head (no eyes/brow/nose — only the skeleton variant gets sockets/jaw), plain sphere-blob hands, and a very simple tricorn, so it reads as a grey-box placeholder rather than a stylized-AAA character. This is directly in frame during normal on-deck play, so it undercuts the 'crew quality' bar the overhauled ship/ocean now set.
findings.where: test-results/audit-noon2/ship-1-brigantine-deck.png — red-coated figure at the helm, dead center foreground.
findings.root_cause_guess: src/client/core/Game.ts makePlayerMesh (251+): coatMat/clothMat are flat MeshStandardMaterial single colors with no map (275-280); pirate head is a bare skinMat sphere with facial detail only added under `if (isSkeleton)` (408-432); hands are plain SphereGeometry (333-340, 354-361).
findings.suggested_fix: Add minimal face detail for the pirate variant (small dark eye quads/brow + simple nose like the skeleton path already does), give the coat a cheap albedo/normal or at least a belt/trim/seam accent mesh, and shape the hands (small box mitts or scaled spheres). Or, if the low-poly look is intentional, pull the deck camera back a bit so the mannequin fidelity isn't front-and-center.

findings.title: Opponent nameplates punch through ship geometry and are oversized at close range
findings.what: Nearby opponents' name billboards ('Pirate_1', 'Pirate_3') render with depth testing disabled and a high render order, so they draw straight through your own sails, masts and hull — the label floats over the middle of your deck/sail instead of over the far player. At close range the 3.4-world-unit-wide sprite is also huge, spanning roughly half the ship. It reads as a debug overlay rather than a diegetic HUD element.
findings.where: test-results/audit-noon2/ship-1-brigantine-deck.png ('Pirate_1' overprinting the mainsail/helm), test-results/audit-noon2/ship-3-sloop-deck.png ('Pirate_3' over the deck), ship-1/ship-2 ext shots.
findings.root_cause_guess: src/client/core/Game.ts:961 makeNameplateSprite sets SpriteMaterial depthTest:false and :965 renderOrder 998; :962 fixed sprite.scale 3.4 with no distance falloff; shown for any alive opponent within 85m (:7919).
findings.suggested_fix: Enable depthTest (or add a soft occlusion fade) so plates don't punch through solid geometry, and scale the sprite down / clamp its apparent size with distance so close opponents don't get a giant label. Consider hiding plates for players on the same ship as the camera.
